_comment: What this was last verified against, and the reason the file exists.
The kernel module in contrib/npuep is C against one kernel's headers. When OPNsense moves to
a new FreeBSD, the installed module stops loading - and because the boot hook is written to
exit 0 rather than block a boot, the appliance comes up quietly with no front ports. The
silence is deliberate and it is also how this would go unnoticed.
So: .github/workflows/upstream.yml watches for a new OPNsense release and raises an issue
when one appears, and install/verify.sh is what to run on the appliance afterwards. Update
the fields below only after verify.sh passes on real hardware.
board: Sophos XGS 136, assembly AMDA0201, Marvell CN9131, 14 ports
verified_how: install/verify.sh on the appliance, after a cold boot, with the driver loaded by the boot hook
version_sensitive: contrib/npuep/*.c - rebuild required on any FreeBSD version change
src/etc/rc.syshook.d/early/* - depends on OPNsense running early syshooks before it configures interfaces
